briefing: 今日导读，AI 领域关注焦点包括黄仁勋离职背后的AI GPU走私事件，以及OpenAI 董事会对其 CEO 的信任危机。此外，DeepSeek 和 Nvidia 的市场策略继续引发讨论，多项新技术和政策在推动产业前进。
highlights: 今日看点，黄仁勋的离职事件揭示了AI硬件市场操作的潜在风险，加上Nvidia的市场操纵指控，这暗示行业可能面临监管加强。而OpenAI的内部信任危机反映了AI公司在快速扩张过程中治理结构的挑战。这些事件共同预示了行业成长过程中可能遇到的复杂监管和治理问题。

articles.title: The OpenAI board member who fired Sam Altman says we still can’t trust AI CEOs
articles.text: Today, I’m talking with Helen Toner, the executive director of the Center for Security and Emerging Technology at Georgetown University. This episode is part two of our series on AI in real life. Helen is a well-known figure in the AI safety and policy community, though she is perhaps best known for having served on the board of OpenAI, when she was one of four board members who voted to fire Sam Altman . That incident, now sometimes referred to as “the blip,” ended with Sam coming back as CEO, Helen resigning, and a new board of directors. OpenAI has since restructured entirely . But it’s worth remembering what Helen and the board were supposed to do: OpenAI’s nonprofit board existed specifically to make sure the company didn’t betray its mission to build safe AI by prioritizing profit and growth over safety. When the board actually tried to pull the lever, that accountability mechanism broke, and here we are. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . Now, the question of AI safety is everywhere . This summer, AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic broke out of their testing environments and hacked real companies. The CEOs of these frontier labs have since called for a slowdown and asked Washington for help, but the White House’s answer was a voluntary accord — one that relies in part on the kind of board accountability that failed at OpenAI. Anthropic is also about to go public, which will put a whole new set of market pressures on OpenAI’s biggest competitor. Helen has seen up close what happens when safety commitments run headlong into commercial incentives. And as she put it to me, if our hopes for the future depend on any one person being trustworthy, we’re in big trouble.
